matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any matchstick, compute the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy that must be corrected. This gives a target change that any valid stick move must achieve.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the very beginning, before any stick moves are considered.
matchstick.example: Skipping the initial calculation and arbitrarily moving a stick, resulting in an equation that still doesn't balance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved to turn a Roman numeral or operator into another valid Roman numeral or operator, including both removal from one character and addition to another. Considering all such transformations ensures no viable move is missed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After knowing the required numeric correction, during the generation of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Only checking moves that relocate sticks from numerals to other numerals, missing a move that changes a '+' into '-' and adds an I.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: Select a stick move whose effect on the numeric values (increase or decrease) exactly matches the required discrepancy, taking into account changes to numerals and operators. Only moves that produce the exact needed correction can lead to a correct equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating each candidate move, compare its numeric impact to the needed correction.
matchstick.example: Choosing a move that changes the total by 2 while the discrepancy is 1, leading to a false equality.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, verify that each resulting character is a legal Roman numeral or a valid operator (+, -, =). Reject any move that creates an illegal symbol before checking the arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after applying a candidate move, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: After moving a stick, ending up with a single diagonal line (not a valid Roman numeral) and accepting it.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character repositioning
matchstick.principle: Allow a stick to be moved within the same character to change its shape (e.g., reposition a diagonal stick to turn V into X) without affecting other characters. Intra‑character repositioning can produce valid new symbols that are otherwise overlooked.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, include moves that keep the stick within its original character.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning V into X by repositioning a diagonal stick within the same character.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Consider taking a horizontal stick from the '=' sign (or adding one) to turn it into a '-' sign, or moving a horizontal stick onto a '-' to turn it into '=', ensuring both operators remain valid. Operator changes of this kind can adjust the arithmetic relationship without altering numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests changing the equality operator, or when a horizontal stick can be transferred between operators.
matchstick.example: Not considering that removing a horizontal stick from '=' could turn it into '-', thus overlooking a valid operator change.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: Consider moving the vertical stick of a '+' sign to turn it into a '-' sign, or adding a vertical stick to a '-' to turn it into '+', while keeping the operators valid. Changing addition to subtraction (or vice versa) often resolves the numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests changing addition to subtraction (or vice versa), or when a vertical stick can be transferred between '+' and '-'.
matchstick.example: Overlooking that removing the vertical stick from '+' yields '-', missing a potential solution.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, allow it to be taken from one character (numeral or operator) and placed onto another, ensuring both source and target characters remain valid after the move. Cross‑character relocation expands the set of possible corrections beyond intra‑character changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, allow sticks to be relocated across characters.
matchstick.example: Restricting moves to within a single character and never moving a stick from one character to another, missing cross‑character solutions.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Consider moving a stick directly from one operator to another operator, simultaneously transforming both operators into other valid operators (e.g., moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' to swap them). Operator‑to‑operator relocation can resolve discrepancies by altering the operation signs on both sides of the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When both source and target characters are operators, explicitly consider moving a stick between them.
matchstick.example: Failing to consider moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' to swap them, missing the solution 'VII - I = VI'.
